overview: White plays 3.c4 against the ...e6 Sicilian, aiming for a Maroczy-style bind with Nc3, d4 and a clamp on d5, rather than the open Sicilian. Black can play ...Nc6 and ...Nf6 or ...d5, striking at the centre. I am not certain of the theory, but it is a rare, quiet anti-Sicilian where White seeks space and a lasting positional edge.

white_ideas.idea: Set up c4, e4, Nc3 and d4, keeping a Maroczy-style grip on d5.
Develop Be2 and O-O and play on the queenside with b4 and Rb1.

black_ideas.idea: Strike with ...Nc6 and ...d5 or ...Nf6 to challenge e4 and the centre.
Develop ...b6 and ...Bb7 and ...Nc6, aiming for a Hedgehog-like set-up.

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian pawns with White on c4/e4 and Black on c5/e6, a Maroczy or Hedgehog-like structure.

character.notes: Quiet space-gaining anti-Sicilian with no forcing lines.

soundness.notes: Sound, a legitimate if rare anti-Sicilian.

structure.notes: Asymmetrical Sicilian centre with a half-open d-file after exchanges.
